In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation and focusing properties of surface plasmonic waves on planar circular gratings milled into a thin metal film.

the development of plasmonic nanostructures that can be used for the generation of surface plasmonic waves, and the focusing of these waves to sub-wavelength dimensions for the purpose of enhancing the optical fields in the focal region.
the development of a new class of plasmonic devices for the generation and focusing surface plasmon waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the circular grating is a promising candidate for the generation of SPPs and their focusing.

the use of circular gratings for SPP generation and focusing is an efficient and simple technique to achieve high enhancement factors at the focal point, with a potential to achieve even higher enhancement factors with the use of a more complex phase-matched grating design.
we have demonstrated the generation and focusing, with a circular grating, of surface plasmonic waves from normally incident radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated a plasmonic lens with an effective focal length of 2.4 µm at 532 nm and an enhancement factor of more than 10x over the in-plane field component of a single ring.

we have demonstrated that the circular grating structure is capable of generating and focusing SPP waves from normally incident plane waves, which has been verified by both experimental measurements and theoretical analysis.
we have shown that the plasmonics can be utilized to achieve the focusing of SPPs in the near field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple circular grating can be used to generate and focus surface plasmons, and that the focusing can be tuned to a particular wavelength of SPPs.
the plasmon lens is capable of generating and focusing SPP waves with a high degree of efficiency and that the plasmons can be focused to a spot size of less than the wavelength of light.
a circular grating can focus surface plasmon waves in a manner analogous to the focusing of light with a lens.
